appraisal_events.evidence: il opposait celui d'Odette, bonne, naïve, éprise d'idéal, presque si incapable de ne pas dire la vérité
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann's free indirect thought reverses an old discrediting rumor about Odette (a kept woman of perverse character) with a warm characterization of her as good, naive, idealistic, and almost unable to lie. The stance is uncertain because the very next anecdote shows her constructing an elaborate lie for the Verdurins, complicating whether the passage endorses Swann's idealization.

status_effects.explanation: Swann's local reassessment casts Odette as good-natured and honest, mildly elevating her character in his eyes, though the immediate anecdote about her lying to Mme Verdurin tempers how firmly this can be read as a stable positive judgment.

ambiguities: Swann's praise of Odette as nearly incapable of lying is immediately followed by an episode where she does lie elaborately (to the Verdurins), which the passage frames sympathetically (her visible discomfort) but which structurally undercuts the praise; scored conservatively with uncertain narrative stance.
M. Vinteuil is referenced only as the composer of the sonata ('la petite phrase de la sonate de Vinteuil'); he does not appear as a social participant in this passage, so he was not scored.
Mme Verdurin appears only as the addressee of Odette's invented excuse and asks a solicitous question; the passage does not stage an evaluative event about her own status, so she was not scored.
M. Verdurin and Rémi are not distinctly present in this passage text (only the collective 'les Verdurin' and 'Mme Verdurin' appear), so they were omitted.
